# Arkansans for Pension Integrity

Arkansans for Pension Integrity is a statewide campaign for transparent, financially sound stewardship of Arkansas public retirement money.

## Current public account

- Arkansas agencies completed at least $65 million in Israel Bonds purchases: $50 million at the State Treasury and $15 million at APERS.
- ATRS separately moved $50 million into a Reams manager account created for an Israel Bonds strategy. The released account documents do not list the individual bonds held in that account.
- The $115 million combined figure means completed purchases plus manager funding. It is not a single holdings total.
- A later $10 million Treasury payment record showed the bank still processing the transaction, so the amount is not included in the completed-purchase total.
- ATRS and APERS authorized a combined ceiling of up to $100 million. An authorization ceiling is not a purchase total.
- Aon advised ATRS on implementation and manager selection and recommended Reams. Aon did not advise whether ATRS should invest or which bond to buy.
- APERS's chief investment officer wrote that he prepared no Board material on the investment and believed the consultants had not either.
- Treasury's October 2024 internal overview recommended holding existing positions; Treasury later settled $20 million in new positions in May 2025.

## Policy proposal

The Pension Investment Integrity Act would require a written credit analysis, alternatives comparison, liquidity disclosure, and fiduciary determination for future covered pension purchases of non-tradable sovereign debt. It is issuer-neutral, prospective, and leaves investment outcomes with pension trustees. Citizens First Congress selected pension investment integrity as a short-term priority for the 2027 Arkansas legislative session.
